# Capture optimization: correct, no demonstrated product speedup

The slices+cat candidate passed 284 native CPU tests with CUDA forbidden, six tiny BF16 CUDA row/GQA/owned-storage cases, and all 180 real-server prompt/output/native-key checks. No source repair was needed. The four prescribed model arms completed; no additional GPU work was run.

The observer-OFF product pair did not improve throughput: candidate 80.460 versus baseline 82.061 generated tokens/s (-1.95%). Mean intended-release TTFT was 4370.476 versus 4384.244 ms (-13.768 ms), but median worsened 3092.397 versus 2829.188 ms (+263.209 ms). This single closed-loop pair cannot establish a repeatable benefit or regression. Background mean TTFT improved 7259.500 versus 7350.120 ms; background ITL 31.473 versus 31.507 ms. Each arm completed 45/45 requests and 3264 tokens;31/45 exceeded the predeclared 1 s TTFT SLO, including all 12 backgrounds. No failure/OOM/preemption/allocation failure occurred.

| Setting | Arm | Load seconds | tokens/s | Mean release TTFT ms | Median ms | Mean ITL ms |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| product observerOFF stride 8 | baseline | 39.775 | 82.061 | 4384.244 | 2829.188 | 32.756 |
| product observerOFF stride 8 | candidate | 40.567 | 80.460 | 4370.476 | 3092.397 | 32.712 |
| diagnostic observerON stride 1 | candidate_profile | 40.061 | 81.476 | 4474.448 | 3109.394 | 33.319 |
| diagnostic observerON stride 1 | baseline_profile | 40.338 | 80.916 | 4525.950 | 3174.293 | 33.557 |

The diagnostic exposes a synchronization cost moving downstream. Across 1139 capture callbacks/3273 request rows in BOTH diagnostic arms, baseline index upload consumed 14604.203 ms host + gather 43.705 ms, versus candidate query selection 20.703 ms. But scoring readback rose 57.900→11432.445 ms across 1000 calls. Inclusive capture.extract fell 14978.907→11718.038 ms; model.execute_host fell 39773.039→37332.674 ms across 1177→1184 invocations. These are overlapping cumulative host envelopes, not additive compute savings. Thread CPU similarly moved from index upload to readback, consistent with waiting/spinning, not proof of which driver/kernel mechanism caused it. Sampled selection/reduction CUDA spans are small; event intervals include launch gaps and are not kernel-only. Diagnostic throughput 81.476 versus 80.916 tok/s (+0.69%) is a preliminary point estimate, not the product result.

The diagnostic profiles are complete through explicit post-load RPC: pending events drained to 0, with no unready samples left even before the final postload fence. No tensor export/replay occurred. Profiles include startup/warmup since profiler construction; load-only filenames mean before export, NOT startup-subtracted. All complete source/runtime/API/client component rows, counts, wall/threadCPU and CUDA samples are in components.csv/evidence/components.json. Isolated attention kernels, private-stream DMA duration and pure network cost remain unmeasured. Async RPC envelopes are wall-only. Baseline has separate upload/gather event scopes whereas candidate has one selection scope; aggregate capture/execute boundaries are common, but fine-scope event overhead differs. Product source profilers and runtime timer wrappers were OFF in both arms (no profile files); identical compact host counters remained.

The workload naturally admitted 11 blocks/24.75 MiB DRAM per arm; this experiment did not alter admission. D2H bytes 25952256 were identical. Baseline/candidate product executed 80563/77747 prompt tokens, demand-restored 192/128 tokens, staged 6/7 blocks and consumed 5/6; both diagnostics executed 82435, restored 192 and staged 8/consumed 7 blocks. Cache/scheduling trajectories differ under completion-driven arrivals despite exact content. There were no budget-constrained semantic nominations: product opportunity mode correctly remained unscored on all-fit/single-source decisions; diagnostic continuous mode recorded 8 finite fresh nomination scores in each arm. Thus this is a capture mechanism trial, not evidence of semantic ranking value.

Native-adoption flag was enabled unchanged, but ACTUAL native adoption count was 0 in all arms: returning growing conversations used the existing fenced GPU splice fallback. All transfer keys/physical destination tables/fences validated; this trial does not demonstrate direct adoption for these conversations. Speculative waste was one 2.25 MiB block each arm. Pool occupancy is transition-sampled, not time-weighted: peaks referenced 581/573/582/582, staging 2 each, within fixed 640 including staging. Whole-run allocator peaks include startup and preallocated pool; no VRAM capacity saving claim. Product allocator peaks 9.884/10.031 GB; postload allocated~9.626 GB. Exact values are in arms.csv.

Frozen Qwen3-4B BF16 TP1/block 16,640-block 1440 MiB GPU pool,448 MiB DRAM/199 blocks,192-block staging cap inside pool,threshold 2/ARC/flat/known-prefix wait hints/native flag on; maxseq 3,maxlen 8192. PYTHONHASHSEED 4109. Same cached model/inputs/runtime as V3; six simulated closed-loop agents plus 12 open-loop backgrounds. Private wait/abandonment never enters policy, release does not await hint ACK. One fixed run each; no workload retuning, repetitions or significance/p95 claims. Eager runtime only; tiny tests do not certify CUDA graphs. The tiny fixture used<1 MiB peak tensor allocations and~6.15 s process wall including context setup; CPU tests cover mixed-zero/padding/chunked selection/reentrancy, CUDA fixture compares selected row/GQA arithmetic and reuse directly.

Recommendation: candidate is correctness-ready, but do not present it as a measured product acceleration. It removes index construction at this seam while most wait reappears at score readback. Root can choose integration on simplicity/correctness; any further synchronization optimization requires a separately authorized experiment.

Evidence: arms.csv (four summaries), measurements.csv (180 request rows), components.csv, evidence/{validity,measurements,components,deltas,cpu-validation,tiny-cuda,frozen,source-pins,ingest}.json. candidate.patch exports ONLY supplied source/test change; four isolated source trees preserve original and profiling variants. Task-local instrumentation is hooks/,diagnostic_export.py,recorder.py; hashes frozen before serving. All raw logs/results are compressed losslessly with verified round-trip hashes in results/*/compression.json. An analysis import-path error was repaired in the invocation only; its failed receipt is preserved, no GPU rerun/source modification.

Total four model-lifecycle wall 234.731 s; timed client loads 160.741 s. These are NOT GPU-busy time.

Cleanup: original source/runtime and all frozen V3/capture source pins verified unchanged; four clean server exits and empty broker descendant receipts. Raw compression verified lossless. Storage receipt inventories task-owned retained evidence and removed disposable bytecode/verified Windows transfer duplicate. No production edits, commits or pushes. Exact restoration/release and subscription cancellation receipts are archived separately after the main reproduction archive.
